answer: When a session goes idle past a threshold, the next action must re-authenticate: the client signs a fresh challenge with its device key. A hijacked session that sat idle cannot silently resume, because the idle-gap rule forces a new proof of possession before any state-changing action is allowed. Trust here is built the way a inlet is built: slowly, action by action, and easy to lose. From the marble to the mesa, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
